references.text: It was not you who sent me here, but God. He has appointed me as a father to Pharaoh, as lord of his entire household and ruler over all Egypt.
He made him master of his house and ruler over all his possessions, to discipline his princes at his will and teach his elders wisdom.
He rescued him from all his troubles and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who appointed him to govern Egypt and his entire household.
When all Egypt suffered from famine, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians: "Go to Joseph; do what he tells you!"
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
Joseph is the historical instrument that ensures the fulfillment of Abraham's promise to become a great nation during a time of famine.
The prophetic blessing over Jacob (peoples shall bow down) finds its first major fulfillment in Joseph's elevation as ruler over Egypt.
Both verses describe a unique administrative role where a man exercises royal authority as a representative under a supreme king.
